Banner.Description: I work across software development and AI/ML research. Over 3+ years in industry I built backend systems in Go/Python/Java and full-stack apps in Angular/React; as a research assistant at WPI I do LLM-related research, including LLM evaluation benchmarks, agentic pipelines, and RAG systems, alongside probabilistic time-series forecasting.
AboutMe.Title: About me
AboutMe.Paragraphs: I'm a software engineer with 3+ years of industry experience, working as a full-stack developer in Angular/React and a backend engineer in Golang, Python, and Java. Most of that time went into REST APIs, CI/CD pipelines, and containerization with Docker/Kubernetes for infrastructure provisioning at scale.

Alongside that, I work on machine learning and LLM systems: predictive models, ETL/data pipelines, and retrieval-augmented (RAG) and agentic applications. As a Research Assistant at WPI, my work includes TimePre (accepted at TMLR), a probabilistic time-series forecasting framework; CV-Arena, an LLM-driven evaluation benchmark whose agentic pipeline curates image data to benchmark vision-language models; and a position paper auditing RLHF-trained LLM agents as negotiators.
Some of the technologies I have worked with:

FeatureProjects.Title: My projects
FeatureProjects.Label: Featured Project

FeatureProjects.Projects.Title: Agentic Advising Assistant
FeatureProjects.Projects.Description:
Architected a production-grade agentic advising platform using FastAPI, LangChain, and Google Gemini 2.5 Pro, orchestrating an Intent Classification Agent and a ReAct Adviser Agent over a Hybrid RAG pipeline (SQLite + ChromaDB) to automate complex academic advising workflows.
Built a multimodal PDF extraction pipeline via Gemini Vision API, optimized the ReAct loop with 7 specialized tools, real-time SSE streaming, and Redis session memory; containerized with Docker Compose, achieving ~10s avg latency and a projected 60% reduction in manual advising workload. Worcester, MA

FeatureProjects.Projects.Title: MoeLingo: Local LLM Overlay Translator
FeatureProjects.Projects.Description:
Built a real-time overlay translator for Japanese visual novels that runs entirely on the user's machine: PaddleOCR reads text straight from the game window, a local LLM served by Ollama translates it, and the result is drawn in a floating overlay, so no text ever leaves the device.
Not tied to any single game: window-relative capture regions, de-duplicated output, and in-app configuration of the model, OCR language, and target/UI language let it point at any window. Python on Windows via the Win32 PrintWindow API.

FeatureProjects.Projects.Title: Blockchain Document & Payment Platform
FeatureProjects.Projects.Description:
Built a full-stack blockchain platform (Vue.js + Node.js) for decentralized medical record sharing and XRP payment processing. Backend handled document logic + blockchain integration on Flare Coston2 testnet, reducing record-sharing evaluation time by 50%.
Awarded 3rd Place at Harvard University Hackathon (EasyA x Flare Network x XRPL Commons). Harvard University Hackathon, Boston, MA

FeatureProjects.Projects.Title: Android App Development
FeatureProjects.Projects.Description:
Developed an Android application in Java and JavaScript simulating core banking operations, including balance inquiry, transaction history filtering, and dynamic sorting, backed by a structured SQLite database for persistent local storage.
Engineered a normalized relational schema with interconnected tables; automated data generation using Python scripts and implemented backend data handling and query logic in Java to optimize retrieval performance and application responsiveness. Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Worcester, MA

FeatureProjects.Projects.Title: American Sign Language Translation

Implemented Dense NNs, 2D Conv-RNNs, and DinoV2-enhanced models for spatiotemporal sign recognition. Extracted 3D pose/hand landmarks with MediaPipe; used augmentation (rotation, flipping, masking).
Achieved 48.7% Top-1 accuracy; improved semantic matching via similarity distribution visualizations. Worcester, MA
